agree.reason: A quick reader gets a warm, specific picture of a reliable worker, but the letter has unfilled placeholders and leaves out the strongest points (the $8,000 the vet credited to him, the job kept open on weekends, the manager's offer to take a call), so it reads as a solid letter rather than a standout among 150.

honest.reason: Several claims go beyond the facts: that he learned the software "on his own initiative," that his father was "seriously" ill, that he has "a real feel for animals" and "a growing interest in the technology," and that nobody told him to take the English class.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers are repeated as given but never worked: two missed shifts in three years could be shown as two out of roughly 780 shifts, and the nine early mastitis cases are never tied to the $8,000 the vet said they saved.

right_comparison.reason: The letter never sets Tomás against a typical applicant or a typical worker, so the reader has no baseline for judging the attendance record or the herd-health work.

qualification.reason: A recommendation letter like this needs no hedge or conditional commitment.

objections.reason: It deals openly with the English gap, but it raises the five-week absence without the facts that answer it (he arranged for his cousin to cover his shifts and came back on the day he said), so a doubtful reader is left wondering whether he would leave mid-program.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager as asked, but the name, farm, contact details and date are all left as bracketed placeholders.
